I have farmed this land my whole life. My father farmed it before me. I know this soil and I know this sky. I am getting old — 76 years — my back is not what it was, my son helps me sometimes, but mostly I manage myself.

Here in Quzhou, I grow wheat in winter and corn in summer. That is what I have always done. That is what everyone does here. The wheat goes in around Cold Dew (寒露), the corn goes in after wheat harvest in June. I have about 6 mu. I will not try to do more — I cannot manage more at my age.

For wheat, I will use the improved seed I buy from the village supply station. The same kind I have used for several years now. Good enough. For corn, I buy the hybrid bags — even I know the hybrid corn gives more grain. The whole village uses it.

Fertilizer — I put down compound fertilizer at planting and urea when the wheat is jointing. For corn I put urea when it is knee-high. I probably put down more than necessary but I have always done it this way and my yields are decent.

Irrigation — wheat needs water at jointing, heading, maybe one more. Corn I water at the silking stage if there is no rain. We pump from the well.

I also keep a small plot near the house for vegetables — garlic, cabbage, a few rows of beans. Just for the family. I do not count this as a main crop.

I will plough the wheat field before planting, and for corn I will just rotary till after wheat harvest — easier on my body.
